licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These ten buckets cleanly partition the observed distribution by mapping each item to its dominant harm type: fraud in obtaining licenses or practicing, criminal history, substandard or negligent clinical care, substance-driven impairment, non-substance physical/mental incapacity, aiding or being an unlicensed practitioner, misleading advertising, fee-splitting/overbilling/financial fraud, administrative non-compliance (continuing education, reporting, record-keeping, board orders), and sexual abuse or analogously serious patient-safety misconduct.

profession_specific.laser_procedures_aut.rationale: The items cluster naturally around the three most-named specific procedures (capsulotomy, trabeculoplasty, iridotomy), plus a few states grant broad or general laser authority, one state limits lasers to diagnostics/imaging, and a small residual group (light adjustable lens, cosmetic exclusions) fits an Other catch-all.

profession_specific.minor_surgical_proce.rationale: These eight buckets cover the dominant clusters in the data: superficial foreign body removal (the most common), epilation of eyelashes, corneal scraping/debridement/puncture, lacrimal probing/dilation/irrigation/plug insertion, injections (anaphylaxis, steroids, botulinum toxin, etc.), eyelid lesion excision/chalazion/laceration repair, light-based or device therapies (IPL, thermal, biologic membranes), and a residual bucket for items like suture removal, blood collection, and vaccine administration.

profession_specific.controlled_substance.rationale: The data clusters naturally around DEA schedule-level prohibitions (I and II being banned most often), a recurring hydrocodone/combination-drug carve-out from Schedule II bans, permissive rules for lower schedules (III–V) with or without supply-day caps, route-of-administration or drug-class exclusions (injectables, opioids, immunosuppressives), and a small group of states that ban all controlled substances entirely, giving seven non-overlapping buckets that cover every row.
